cues.s6|Flexure formula: Stress is linear in y, a seesaw pivoting on the neutral axis. Units: N·m × m / m⁴ = N/m².
cues.s6|Moment-curvature relation: Hooke's law for bending: moment equals stiffness EI times the bend κ. Small slopes make κ simply w″.
cues.s6|Euler-Bernoulli beam equation: Climb the derivative ladder: w, slope, curvature (M), shear, load. Four derivatives, four boundary conditions, two per end.
cues.s6|Section properties: Depth gets the cube in bh³/12; circle is πr⁴/4; parallel axis always adds area times distance squared.
cues.s6|Principal axes: Mohr's circle pattern: tan 2θ is twice the product of inertia over the difference of the diagonals, with a minus sign on top.
cues.s6|Standard deflections: Cantilever 3 and 8; simply supported 48 and 384 with a 5 on top. Point load with L³, uniform load with wL⁴.
cues.s7|Open-section shear flow: Shear flow accumulates from the free edge like water collecting: q tracks the first moment Q swept so far, scaled by V/I.
cues.s7|Bredt-Batho: Each wall element gives moment q r ds = q × 2dA, twice its swept triangle; summed around the cell, T = 2Aq.
cues.s7|Closed-cell twist and J: Check with a circular tube: 4(πR²)²/(2πR/t) = 2πR³t, the thin-tube polar moment. Equal θ′ in every cell.
cues.s7|Thin open-section torsion: Each strip is a thin rectangle worth bt³/3; thickness cubed makes open sections floppy. Peak stress in the thickest strip.
cues.s7|Circular shaft torsion: Same shape as σ = My/I. Polar J = πd⁴/32 is twice the bending I = πd⁴/64.
cues.s7|Prandtl stress function: Soap film on the section inflated by 2Gθ′: slope gives stress, twice the volume gives torque.
cues.s8|Strain energy of a slender member: Every term is load squared over twice its stiffness, matching a spring's P²/(2k): M with EI, N with EA, T with GJ.
cues.s8|Castigliano's second theorem: Force in, displacement out. Spring check: U = P²/(2k) gives ∂U/∂P = P/k.
cues.s8|Unit load method: Real moment times unit-load moment over stiffness, integrated. Aim the unit load along the displacement you want.
cues.s8|Minimum total potential energy: Ball in a bowl: equilibrium where the landscape is flat, stable where it curves upward.
cues.s8|Rayleigh-Ritz: Trial shapes with amplitudes as tuning knobs; minimizing Π over the knobs gives a small stiffness system Ka = f.
cues.s8|Maxwell-Betti reciprocity: Swap the load point and the measuring point and the deflection is the same: a symmetric flexibility matrix.
cues.s9|Energy stability criterion: First derivatives zero for equilibrium; the Hessian determinant reaches zero where the bowl flattens, at the critical load.
cues.s9|Rigid bar with rotational spring: Spring stores ½Cθ², load drops by L(1 − cos θ). Linearize: (C − PL)θ = 0 gives P_cr = C/L.
cues.s9|Rigid bar with lateral spring: Spring stretches L sin θ; the lever arm L cos θ shrinks as the bar tilts, so P = kL cos θ falls.
cues.s9|Multi-DOF linear eigenproblem: Vibration twin of det(K − ω²M) = 0, with geometric stiffness K_G in place of mass and P in place of ω².
cues.s9|Koiter post-buckling expansion: Slope a decides asymmetric; curvature b decides symmetric: positive b smiles (stable), negative b frowns (unstable).
cues.s9|Imperfection sensitivity laws: Unstable symmetric: two-thirds power. Asymmetric: one-half power, the square root, the steeper drop for small ε.
cues.s10|Degree of indeterminacy: Unknowns minus equations: truss members bring 1 force and joints give 2 equations; frame members bring 3 and joints give 3.
cues.s10|Force method compatibility: Cut the redundant, measure the gap from the loads, close it with X₁ times its flexibility: total gap zero.
cues.s10|Springs in series and parallel: Series shares force, so compliances add. Parallel shares displacement, so stiffnesses add.
cues.s10|Member stiffnesses: Axial EA/L, torsion GJ/L; bending scales as EI/L³: cantilever 3, fixed-fixed midspan 192 (four times 48).
cues.s10|Bar element stiffness: Rows sum to zero because a rigid translation stores zero energy; pull one node and the other feels the opposite.
cues.s10|Classic indeterminate results: Propped cantilever: 3/8 at the prop, 5/8 at the wall. Fixed-fixed: wL²/12 at the ends, half that at midspan.
cues.s11|Curved beam bending energy: Ordinary M²/(2EI) energy with ds = R dθ; the quarter ring gives π/4 times PR³/(EI).
cues.s11|Winkler curved beam stress: Hyperbolic in r: the 1/r factor loads the inner fiber; r_n sits a distance e inside the centroid.
cues.s11|Transformed section: Scale the width, keep the depth: the stiffer material widens by n, then its stress is multiplied back by n.
cues.s11|Modulus-weighted bending: Weight every area by its modulus, then run the usual centroid and parallel-axis formulas with E inside.
cues.s11|Parallel axial members: Bonded bars share one strain, like parallel springs: each takes its EA share of the load.
cues.s11|Sandwich bending stiffness: Two faces, each area bt at distance d/2: 2E_f bt(d/2)² = E_f btd²/2, an I-beam couple.
cues.s14|Euler buckling load: π² over effective length squared: a cantilever (K = 2) carries a quarter of the pinned load, fixed-fixed (K = 0.5) four times.
cues.s14|Beam-column equation: Bending term w⁗ plus axial term Pw″; k² = P/(EI) makes sin kx and cos kx the buckled shapes.
cues.s14|Imperfection amplification: Geometric series 1 + P/P_cr + (P/P_cr)² + …: each pass of P times deflection adds more bending.
cues.s14|Southwell plot: Rearranged amplification: plot δ/P against δ; slope is 1/P_cr, intercept is δ₀/P_cr.
cues.s14|Secant formula: Eccentricity ratio ec/r² times a secant whose argument reaches π/2 exactly at P = P_cr, where stress grows unbounded.
cues.s14|Johnson parabola: Starts at σ_y for zero slenderness and touches the Euler curve at σ_y/2; the 4π²E denominator sets that tangency.
